passage: Devika had just finished presenting her poster at the department seminar when Dr Manjula said from the back row, "A bit ambitious for a second-year, don't you think?" The room laughed. Two weeks earlier Manjula had praised the very same data. Since Devika's abstract was accepted for the national meeting, her lab-meeting slots had shrunk, and the shared microscope booking kept showing Manjula's name against her usual hours. Devika still remembered how Manjula taught her to read a blot, so she answered, "Thank you, Ma'am. I learnt to check my controls from you." Afterwards, in the corridor, she wondered what she had done wrong. On Friday she emailed Professor Rao, a visiting collaborator, asking for feedback on her next draft.

qa.q: What did Dr Manjula say about Devika's poster?
qa.a: Dr Manjula said it was a bit ambitious for a second-year.

qa.q: Why did Devika wonder what she had done wrong in the corridor?
qa.a: Devika was confused, since Manjula had praised the same data two weeks earlier and the change made no sense to her.

qa.q: What did Devika do to keep growing without shrinking?
qa.a: She thanked Manjula for what was taught and reached out to Professor Rao for feedback on her next draft.

qa.q: How might Manjula be feeling as Devika's abstract is accepted?
qa.a: Manjula may feel threatened or overshadowed, though the passage shows only behaviour, not the reason.

grounding: A mentor in a department seems threatened by a mentee's rise and undercuts her; the mentee stays respectful and seeks other guides.

passage:
Vaibhav: Bhavna. weird question. can a mentor get jealous?
Bhavna: of you, bhai? why
Vaibhav: Kapoor sir removed me from the conference panel. two days after the organisers invited me directly
Vaibhav: and in the team meeting he said my research is "still very junior"
Vaibhav: this is the same man who told me last year I was his best student
Bhavna: hmm. did anything change?
Vaibhav: my paper got cited more than his last one. that's all I can think of
Bhavna: that might be it honestly
Vaibhav: I don't get it. I'm confused. I owe him so much 😔
Bhavna: you can still owe him and not shrink yourself
Bhavna: do you have other people you can learn from?
Vaibhav: Dr. Joshi keeps saying I can come to her
Bhavna: go. and keep being respectful to Kapoor sir. just don't turn down invitations to keep him comfortable
Vaibhav: ok. I'll write to the organisers and say I'd still love to speak
Bhavna: that's it 👍

qa.q: What did Kapoor sir remove Vaibhav from?
qa.a: He removed Vaibhav from the conference panel.

qa.q: How does Vaibhav feel about Kapoor sir's behaviour?
qa.a: Vaibhav feels confused and hurt, because he owes his mentor so much.

qa.q: What advice did Bhavna give, and why is it good?
qa.a: To stay respectful, seek other guides like Dr. Joshi, and not turn down opportunities to protect his mentor's ego.

qa.q: How might Kapoor sir be feeling as Vaibhav grows?
qa.a: Kapoor sir may feel threatened and envious that his student is getting more attention than he is.

grounding: A chat shows a young researcher whose mentor seems threatened by his growth and starts blocking him, who keeps respecting him, seeks other guides and does not shrink.

passage:
In the small town of Aldona in Goa, Nazia had learned everything about baking from Maria aunty: how to feel when dough was ready, how to fold butter for puffs. For three years she worked in Maria's bakery at dawn.

Then Nazia started making cakes on her own for weddings, and people began asking for her by name. Maria aunty grew quiet. She told a customer that Nazia's cakes "look nice but taste of nothing". She stopped lending her the big oven.

Nazia didn't understand. Hadn't Maria wanted her to be good?

She cried one evening at her cousin's house, confused and hurt. Her cousin said, "She taught you well. Now you're good enough to scare her."

Nazia did not stop baking. She went to Mrs. Lobo, who ran the church catering, to learn about large orders. She still took Maria aunty her favourite coconut sweets at Christmas and thanked her for the puffs. But she took the wedding orders.

qa.q: What did Maria aunty say about Nazia's cakes?
qa.a: She said they "look nice but taste of nothing".

qa.q: How did Nazia feel when Maria aunty turned cold?
qa.a: Nazia felt confused and hurt, crying at her cousin's house.

qa.q: What did Nazia do that was wise?
qa.a: She kept respecting and thanking Maria aunty, found another guide in Mrs. Lobo, and kept taking wedding orders instead of shrinking.

qa.q: How might Maria aunty feel as customers ask for Nazia by name?
qa.a: Maria aunty probably feels threatened and envious, which shows in her comments and in taking back the oven.

grounding: The passage shows a young woman whose mentor seems threatened by her growth and undercuts her, who keeps respecting her, seeks other guides and does not shrink.
